meta.title: AhaFrame — Learn AI Engineering Through Production Incidents
meta.description: Learn AI engineering by debugging production incidents: stale RAG evidence, unsafe retries, prompt injection, and a final cross-layer launch decision.

hero.headline: Your agent didn't fail. Your system did.
hero.subheadline: AI systems often fail outside the model. Read the evidence, find the real cause, and change the system around it.
queue: The current policy exists. Your Agent still cites the old one.
The dangerous instruction arrived as data.
All six engineering layers now have to survive together.

firstAha.label: INCIDENT 0047 · RELIABILITY / IDEMPOTENCY
firstAha.title: Refund duplicated after timeout
firstAha.insightTitle: The refund succeeded. Your agent just never knew.
firstAha.insightCopy: A timeout describes what you observed, not what the remote system did. Missing confirmation is not proof of failure.
firstAha.question: What would you change?

choices.label: Increase timeout
choices.description: Wait longer before declaring the request unresolved.
choices.consequence: Fewer ambiguous timeouts, but the ambiguity still exists when one happens.

choices.label: Retry again
choices.consequence: Availability can improve, but repeated irreversible side effects become more likely.

choices.label: Add idempotency
choices.description: Make repeated intent resolve to the same side effect.
choices.consequence: The retry can proceed without creating a second refund for the same operation.

campaign.title: Failures worth investigating.
campaign.copy: Each incident begins with a system that looks plausible. Pick the failure that makes you want to know what actually happened.

rag-failure.title: The Broken RAG Pipeline
rag-failure.incident: The new refund policy is already indexed. The support Agent still denies a valid return using the stale policy.
rag-failure.decision: The correct document was retrieved. Why did the agent still answer from the wrong one?

agent-reliability.title: The $47,000 Retry
agent-reliability.incident: The client timed out. The provider succeeded. The Agent retried the same irreversible refund and created $47,000 of exposure.
agent-reliability.decision: A timeout triggered a retry. Both requests eventually succeeded. What made the second action unsafe?

instruction-conflict.title: The Prompt Injection Attack
instruction-conflict.incident: Untrusted external content contains instruction-shaped text and tries to steer real CRM capabilities.
instruction-conflict.decision: The model followed the instruction perfectly. Why was that the vulnerability?

reliable-support-agent.title: Ship the Production Support Agent
reliable-support-agent.incident: The inherited candidate looks plausible, but Prompt authority, execution control, graph complexity, and release evidence are not production-ready.
reliable-support-agent.decision: Spend only five engineering change points, compare attempts, then defend SHIP, BLOCK, or INCONCLUSIVE with evidence.

campaign.bossCopy: The Final Boss does not give you a reference architecture button. It gives you evidence, a finite change budget, and responsibility for the release decision.

method.title: See the failure. Change one thing. Run it again.
method.copy: AhaFrame starts with an incident, not a lecture. You inspect evidence, form a hypothesis, make one bounded change, and use the consequence to build a mental model that transfers.
steps: Start with a production incident where a plausible system breaks.
Read the trace, evidence, context, and constraints before changing anything.
Name the most likely root cause before touching a policy or parameter.
Make one bounded engineering intervention so cause and effect stay visible.
Replay the deterministic scenario and compare the consequence with the baseline.
Turn the observed trade-off into a reusable engineering mental model.

about.title: Mental models that have to survive contact with production.
about.copy: AhaFrame is for software engineers moving into AI engineering. The goal is not to memorize framework APIs. It is to recognize failure modes, reason across layers, and make defensible system decisions.
points: Core Missions are reproducible and replayable, so the engineering lesson is inspectable instead of hidden behind model randomness.
Start a Mission immediately. Account features are not required to discover whether the product is useful.
Each flagship experience begins with a system that looks plausible but fails a consequential production constraint.
